requirement:
Each configurable feature MUST define the name and typed data structure of its
user section and any supported project section, citing these common configuration
requirements. The feature MUST specify its supported keys, value types, defaults,
validation rules, and the precedence or combination rules for user settings,
project settings, and invocation options. It MUST specify the behavior of an
absent section and which operations require that section.

Feature-specific fields MUST stay within the feature's section. A feature MUST
NOT reinterpret another feature's settings or change the shared file locations
or schema version. A feature MAY define a provider-owned options map, but MUST
document that boundary and how those options are validated.
rationale:
## Obligations and coverage

The requirement is satisfied. Its specification obligations are implemented partly by other requirement texts; under the review rules, those texts do not require implementation tests in this review.

| Obligation | Implementation and verification |
|---|---|
| Define each supported user-section name and typed structure. | `requirements.authoring.configuration` names `[authoring]`; `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure` defines `UserAuthoringConfig`. `requirements.configuration.evidence_paths` and `requirements.configuration.workspace_structure` explicitly exclude user counterparts for evidence and coverage. The types are represented by `src/config.rs#struct[UserConfig]` and `src/config.rs#struct[UserAuthoringConfig]`. |
| Define each supported project-section name and typed structure. | `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure` defines `WorkspaceAuthoringConfig`; `requirements.configuration.evidence_paths` names `[evidence]` and `EvidenceConfig`; `requirements.configuration.workspace_structure` names the workspace tables. `src/config.rs#struct[WorkspaceConfig]` reaches `WorkspaceAuthoringConfig`, `EvidenceConfig`, and `CoverageConfig`, defining their typed fields. |
| Cite the common configuration requirements. | The feature requirement texts explicitly reference `requirements.configuration.feature_sections`; authoring additionally cites the common location, structure, and serialization requirements. |
| Specify supported keys. | `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure` and `requirements.authoring.configuration_serialization` enumerate authoring fields and their table placement. `requirements.configuration.evidence_paths` specifies `allow` and `disallow`; `requirements.configuration.workspace_structure` specifies coverage's sole key, `reauthorings`. |
| Specify value types. | The authoring structure text supplies typed records and unions; evidence specifies arrays of literal paths; `requirements.references.coverage.history` specifies a positive integer. The corresponding reachable configuration types agree. |
| Specify defaults. | Authoring's structure, serialization, precedence, and OpenAI-default requirements specify omitted-field behavior and effective defaults. Evidence specifies empty arrays. Coverage history specifies 3 when unset. |
| Specify validation rules. | `requirements.authoring.configuration_storage` specifies name, path, model, environment-variable, and options validation. Evidence specifies nonempty paths, and coverage specifies positivity. The section types reject unknown fields; `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` checks authoring values and protected options. |
| Specify precedence or combination rules for user settings, project settings, and invocation options. | `requirements.authoring.configuration_precedence` specifies invocation selection, user project selection, workspace default, user default, and whole-record workspace overrides. Evidence specifies allow/disallow/default combination rules and explicitly has neither user settings nor invocation options. Coverage likewise has neither a user counterpart nor an invocation option. |
| Specify absent-section behavior. | Authoring's configuration requirement specifies when either section may be absent; evidence specifies empty lists and default access rules; workspace structure and coverage history together specify optional coverage and its fallback. |
| Specify which operations require a section. | `requirements.authoring.configuration` identifies assessments requiring authoring configuration and exempts other operations. Evidence and coverage explicitly require no operation to have their sections. |
| Keep feature-specific fields within their sections. | `src/config.rs#struct[UserConfig]` and `src/config.rs#struct[WorkspaceConfig]` expose only common version and feature tables. Their reachable section/backend types use `deny_unknown_fields`. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[feature_sections_are_scoped_and_absent_sections_use_defaults]` asserts rejection of root-level fields, cross-feature fields, and unsupported user tables. |
| Do not reinterpret another feature's settings. | `src/config.rs#fn[load_workspace_evidence]` decodes and validates evidence independently, without decoding authoring settings. Its credential-presence inspection does not reinterpret those settings. The scoped-sections test loads valid evidence despite invalid, unused authoring settings and asserts the resulting evidence paths. |
| Do not change shared file locations. | `src/config.rs#fn[load_workspace_evidence]` reaches `src/config.rs#fn[workspace_document]`, which performs shared workspace discovery; no feature-specific relocation is introduced. The other marked section types and validators do not select or modify file locations. There is no separate feature-specific transformation here requiring a test. |
| Do not change the shared schema version. | `src/config.rs#fn[validate_workspace_common]` enforces version 1 independently of the feature. The scoped-sections test checks rejection of version 2 with each supported workspace feature present. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[invalid_schema_and_feature_values_report_the_configuration_path]` also checks invalid user versions. |
| Document the provider-owned options boundary. | `requirements.authoring.configuration_serialization` places inference options in `options`; `requirements.authoring.configuration_storage` explicitly makes them backend-defined and prohibits replacement of model, prompt, or tools. |
| Document how provider-owned options are validated. | The storage requirement specifies provider/Rig acceptance and rejection; the structure requirement defines recursive `OptionValue`, including finite floats. `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[validate]` reaches `src/config.rs#impl[OptionValue]/fn[validate]` and rejects protected keys. Both referenced tests exercise forbidden model overrides; the invalid-values test also checks rejection of a nonfinite option. |

The scoped-sections test additionally verifies absent user authoring, absent workspace feature sections, omitted evidence arrays, and the typed coverage setting. The feature-specific specification requirements above carry out the remaining documentary obligations without requiring their own implementations or tests to be reassessed here. No unacknowledged gap or stale acknowledgment was found.

text: :::{req} feature_sections
Each configurable feature MUST define the name and typed data structure of its
user section and any supported project section, citing these common configuration
requirements. The feature MUST specify its supported keys, value types, defaults,
validation rules, and the precedence or combination rules for user settings,
project settings, and invocation options. It MUST specify the behavior of an
absent section and which operations require that section.
Feature-specific fields MUST stay within the feature's section. A feature MUST
NOT reinterpret another feature's settings or change the shared file locations
or schema version. A feature MAY define a provider-owned options map, but MUST
document that boundary and how those options are validated.
:::{req} configuration
Authoring MUST use the `[authoring]` sections of the shared user configuration
and the selected workspace's `habeas.toml`, refining
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the authoring feature.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.user_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.structure`
Assessing a subject with `habeas author`, singly or in a batch that needs at
least one assessment, MUST require an `[authoring]` section in at least one of
these files; either section MAY be absent. No other operation requires the
section, including a batch with no assessments needed and the operations in
{cite}`requirements.authoring.deterministic_validation`.
It MUST support named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local
selection for each project. Credential-source references SHOULD be used;
explicit credentials MUST be supported under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`
:::{req} configuration_structure
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
Habeas MUST define its authoring configuration using these data structures:
```text
UserAuthoringConfig {
default: Optional<ConfigName>,
configs: Map<ConfigName, AuthoringConfig>,
projects: Map<CanonicalProjectRoot, ProjectSelection>,
WorkspaceAuthoringConfig {
default: Optional<ConfigName>,
configs: Map<ConfigName, AuthoringConfig>,  // omitted means empty
ProjectSelection {
config: ConfigName,
AuthoringConfig {
backend: BackendConfig,                   // tagged union, flattened in TOML
concurrency: Optional<PositiveInteger>,   // simultaneous assessments
policy: Optional<AssessmentPolicy>,       // default: Once for OpenAI; Confirm otherwise
AssessmentPolicy = Confirm | Once             // TOML: "confirm" or "once"
BackendConfig = Bedrock(BedrockConfig) | Ollama(OllamaConfig) | Openai(OpenAiConfig)
BedrockConfig {
model: ModelId,                           // model ID or inference-profile ID/ARN
aws_profile: Optional<String>,
region: Optional<String>,
credentials: Optional<BedrockCredentials>,
options: Map<String, OptionValue>,
BedrockCredentials {
access_key_id: SecretString,
secret_access_key: SecretString,
session_token: Optional<SecretString>,
OllamaConfig {
model: ModelId,                           // exact identifier, including tag
endpoint: Optional<String>,               // default: http://localhost:11434
api_key_env: Optional<EnvironmentVariableName>,
api_key: Optional<SecretString>,
options: Map<String, OptionValue>,
OpenAiConfig {
model: Optional<ModelId>,                 // default: gpt-6.1-sol
endpoint: Optional<String>,               // default: https://api.openai.com/v1
api_key_env: Optional<EnvironmentVariableName>, // default: OPENAI_API_KEY
api_key: Optional<SecretString>,
options: Map<String, OptionValue>,
OptionValue = String | Boolean | Integer | FiniteFloat
| Array<OptionValue> | Map<String, OptionValue>
SecretString = String                         // serialized normally; redacted in Debug
ModelRef {
backend: BackendKind,                     // Bedrock, Ollama, or Openai
model: ModelId,
`ModelRef` MUST be derived from the selected backend configuration and MUST
preserve the exact model identifier. It MUST identify the model without replacing
connection settings such as AWS profile, region, or Ollama endpoint.
:::{req} configuration_serialization
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
The user `[authoring]` table MUST serialize UserAuthoringConfig, and the workspace
table MUST serialize WorkspaceAuthoringConfig. Each
`[authoring.configs.<name>]` table MUST serialize one AuthoringConfig, with
`backend = "bedrock"`, `backend = "ollama"`, or `backend = "openai"` and that variant's fields in the same
table. Backend-specific inference options MUST appear in its `options` subtable.
Within a present user authoring section, `configs` MUST be present but MAY be empty;
workspace `configs` MAY be omitted, allowing a workspace default to select a
named user configuration.
omitted `projects` and `options` tables MUST deserialize as empty maps.
Serialization MUST follow the common rules in
{cite}`requirements.configuration.serialization`.
:::{req} openai_defaults
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An OpenAI configuration MAY omit `model`; the effective model MUST then be
`gpt-6.1-sol`. When `options.reasoning.effort` is omitted, the request MUST use
`low` effort, preserving other reasoning options. When `options.max_output_tokens`
is omitted, the request MUST use an output-token limit of 16,384. These option
defaults MUST apply even when the model is overridden. An explicit model,
reasoning effort, or output-token limit MUST override its corresponding default.
Defaults MUST NOT be written into omitted configuration fields on serialization.
An explicitly empty model MUST still be rejected.
:::{req} configuration_storage
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
Configuration names MUST match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and be case-sensitive.
Project-selection keys MUST be canonical absolute project-root paths. Model IDs
MUST be nonempty opaque strings, preserving tags and ARNs. `api_key_env` MUST
name a nonempty environment variable without `=` or NUL.
Authoring MUST validate its fields under {cite}`requirements.configuration.loading`.
The `options` map MUST accept backend-defined inference settings rather than a
closed Habeas list; the adapter MUST pass them through Rig's provider parameter
mechanism and report rejection by Rig or the provider. These options MUST NOT
replace the selected model, the assessment prompt, or tool definitions.
:::{req} configuration_precedence
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`--config <name>` MUST select a configuration for that invocation. Otherwise,
authoring MUST use the user's selection for the canonical project root, then the
workspace default, then the user's default. Named workspace configurations MUST
override same-named user configurations as complete records. Backend, model,
connection settings, and options MUST come from the selected record as a unit;
fields MUST NOT be merged between records. Workspace-only authoring MUST work
without a user configuration file. Missing configuration or an unknown selection
MUST identify the relevant configuration file and point to documented examples.
An explicit Bedrock AWS profile or region MUST override the corresponding SDK
default; omitted values MUST use standard AWS SDK resolution. Ollama MUST use
its configured endpoint or `http://localhost:11434`. If `api_key_env` is set, its
named variable MUST supply the credential; a missing or empty value MUST produce
an error before a model request. OpenAI MUST use its configured endpoint or
`https://api.openai.com/v1`, and MUST resolve `OPENAI_API_KEY` when neither
`api_key` nor `api_key_env` is supplied.
:::{req} workspace_structure
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`habeas.toml` MUST serialize WorkspaceConfig as UTF-8 TOML with `version = 1`.
Its supported feature tables are `[authoring]`, `[coverage]`, and
`[evidence]`; each MAY be absent. `[coverage]` has one optional key,
`reauthorings`, under {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`; it has
no user-file counterpart or invocation option, and no operation requires it. Unknown keys, unsupported versions, and invalid field types MUST produce
a diagnostic identifying the file and setting. Invalid TOML, including content
that is not UTF-8, MUST produce a diagnostic identifying the file, with the line
and column of a syntax error.
Features MUST define their own data structures and loading rules under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`. A file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid. Habeas settings MUST NOT require a `[habeas]` table
inside `book.toml`.
:::{req} evidence_paths
The workspace `[evidence]` table MUST serialize EvidenceConfig. `allow` and
`disallow` MUST be arrays of nonempty literal paths, each naming a file or a
directory subtree. Relative paths MUST resolve from the selected `habeas.toml`
directory; absolute paths MUST be supported. These paths are not glob patterns.
An omitted `allow` or `disallow` MUST mean an empty array, and an absent
`[evidence]` table MUST mean both are empty, so only the default source-access
rules apply. No operation requires the section. The table has no user-file
counterpart, and these rules have no invocation options. This section refines
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the evidence feature.
For authoring reads, a matching disallow MUST reject the path; otherwise a
matching allow MUST permit it; otherwise the default source-access rules MUST
apply. Explicit allow MUST override every default, including Git tracking,
project containment, generated-evidence exclusion, and automatic generated-output
rules. Disallow MUST win even when an allow or generated-output rule also matches.
Both the requested path and its resolved symlink target MUST be checked for
disallow, so an allowed alias cannot expose a disallowed target.
The same explicit disallow rules and external-path exceptions MUST apply when
resolving recorded evidence inputs, including ordinary validation. Validation MUST
remain independent of Git index membership: it
checks the recorded inputs' existence and contents. Loading path policy MUST NOT
resolve credentials or validate unused authoring settings.
:::{req} coverage.history
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{req} documentation
Habeas MUST document the user and project configuration locations, the common
file structure and schema version, and how to create and edit the files by hand.
Each configurable feature MUST document its fields, defaults, resolution rules,
and credential-source references, with complete, copyable examples identifying
all placeholders and the file to edit. Documentation MUST explain how to change
or remove optional settings and selections.
Configuration MUST NOT require a configuration-management command or generated
state beyond the documented files. Primary examples MUST use credential-source
references; examples explaining explicit credential fields MUST use clearly
identified placeholders, never real secrets.
:::{req} evidence_paths
The workspace `[evidence]` table MUST serialize EvidenceConfig. `allow` and
`disallow` MUST be arrays of nonempty literal paths, each naming a file or a
directory subtree. Relative paths MUST resolve from the selected `habeas.toml`
directory; absolute paths MUST be supported. These paths are not glob patterns.
An omitted `allow` or `disallow` MUST mean an empty array, and an absent
`[evidence]` table MUST mean both are empty, so only the default source-access
rules apply. No operation requires the section. The table has no user-file
counterpart, and these rules have no invocation options. This section refines
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the evidence feature.
For authoring reads, a matching disallow MUST reject the path; otherwise a
matching allow MUST permit it; otherwise the default source-access rules MUST
apply. Explicit allow MUST override every default, including Git tracking,
project containment, generated-evidence exclusion, and automatic generated-output
rules. Disallow MUST win even when an allow or generated-output rule also matches.
Both the requested path and its resolved symlink target MUST be checked for
disallow, so an allowed alias cannot expose a disallowed target.
The same explicit disallow rules and external-path exceptions MUST apply when
resolving recorded evidence inputs, including ordinary validation. Validation MUST
remain independent of Git index membership: it
checks the recorded inputs' existence and contents. Loading path policy MUST NOT
resolve credentials or validate unused authoring settings.
:::{req} feature_sections
Each configurable feature MUST define the name and typed data structure of its
user section and any supported project section, citing these common configuration
requirements. The feature MUST specify its supported keys, value types, defaults,
validation rules, and the precedence or combination rules for user settings,
project settings, and invocation options. It MUST specify the behavior of an
absent section and which operations require that section.
Feature-specific fields MUST stay within the feature's section. A feature MUST
NOT reinterpret another feature's settings or change the shared file locations
or schema version. A feature MAY define a provider-owned options map, but MUST
document that boundary and how those options are validated.
:::{req} loading
An operation MUST load user configuration only when its requirements call for
user settings. A missing user file MUST represent absent user configuration;
whether the operation can proceed MUST be defined by the feature. Loading MUST
NOT create a file, repair malformed input, or supply an undocumented selection.
When loading configuration, Habeas MUST report unreadable files, invalid TOML,
unsupported user-file versions, unknown common keys, and invalid common field
types. It MUST validate the feature sections used by that operation and report
invalid feature settings with the file and setting identified. Unknown keys in
an explicitly documented provider-owned options map MUST follow that feature's
validation rules.
An operation MUST NOT require or semantically validate configuration for a
feature it does not use. This isolation MUST NOT suppress TOML syntax errors in
a shared file that the operation otherwise needs to parse. In particular,
ordinary validation still requires a parseable `book.toml` while remaining
independent of authoring settings and the user configuration file. It MUST apply
the selected workspace's evidence path policy without loading its model clients
or credentials.
:::{req} serialization
Saved configuration MUST remain distinct from resolved runtime configuration.
Serializing and deserializing a valid configuration MUST preserve its semantic
values, including explicit versus omitted settings. Optional fields MAY be
omitted on serialization; defaults and environment-derived values MUST NOT be
materialized into omitted fields. TOML comments and formatting need not
round-trip.
Loading configuration or running a configured feature MUST NOT rewrite the user
or project configuration as a side effect. Resolved credentials and live runtime
objects MUST NOT enter the serialized data structures. Explicitly supplied
credential values are permitted only in the fields documented by the authoring
feature; credentials resolved from a profile or environment MUST NOT be written
back to configuration.
:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
:::{req} structure
The user configuration file MUST be UTF-8 TOML serializing UserConfig. It MUST
contain `version = 1` and MAY contain the documented feature tables. The common
root MUST contain only the schema version and those feature tables; feature
settings MUST NOT occupy unscoped root keys. A user file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid common configuration.
Workspace configuration MUST follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`.
The absence of an optional feature section MUST be distinguishable
from that feature's explicit settings and interpreted according to its own
requirements.
:::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
:::{req} workspace_structure
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`

Its supported feature tables are `[authoring]`, `[coverage]`, and

a diagnostic identifying the file and setting. Invalid TOML, including content
that is not UTF-8, MUST produce a diagnostic identifying the file, with the line
and column of a syntax error.
Features MUST define their own data structures and loading rules under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`. A file containing only

inside `book.toml`.
